stem:
Meera finds two identical-looking iron bars in her grandfather's workshop in Jaipur. One is a magnet and the other is a plain iron bar. She has a third bar that she knows is a magnet, with its North pole marked.
Which test will correctly identify which of the two bars is a magnet?

options.text: Bring the North pole of the known magnet near one end of each bar; the bar that is repelled must be a magnet, because like poles repel.
Bring the North pole of the known magnet near one end of each bar; the bar that is attracted must be a magnet, because magnets attract iron.
Hold each bar near some iron nails; both bars will pick up the nails, so either bar could be the magnet.
Bring the North pole of the known magnet near one end of each bar; the bar that is attracted more strongly must be the magnet.

teacher.key_rationale: Attraction alone cannot distinguish a magnet from a plain iron bar, since a magnet attracts both. Only repulsion occurs between like poles of two magnets, so the bar repelled by the known North pole must be a magnet. Options B and D rely on attraction (plain iron is also attracted), and C is false because a plain iron bar does not pick up nails.
